title: Consensus Clustering Analysis Based on Enhanced-CT Radiomic Features: Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma patients' 3-Year Progression-Free Survival.
authors: Jia, Jianye; Liu, Ziyan; Wang, Fen; Bai, Genji
one_liner_zh: 该文基于CT影像组学特征对食管鳞癌患者进行共识聚类以预测无进展生存期，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To assess the efficacy of consensus cluster analysis based on CT radiomics in stratifying risk and predicting postoperative progression-free survival (PFS) in patients diagnosed with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study involving 546 patients diagnosed with ESC between January 2016 and March 2021. All patients underwent preoperative enhanced CT examinations. From the enhanced CT images, radiomics features were extracted, and a consensus clustering algorithm was applied to group the patients based on these features. Statistical analysis was performed to examine the relationship between the clustering results and gene protein expression, histopathological features, and patients' 3-year PFS. We applied the Kruskal-Wallis test for continuous data, chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical data, and the log-rank test for PFS. RESULTS: This study identified four groups: Cluster 1 (n = 100, 18.3%), Cluster 2 (n = 197, 36.1%), Cluster 3 (n = 205, 37.5%), and Cluster 4 (n = 44, 8.1%). The cancer gene Breast Cancer Susceptibility Gene 1 (BRCA1) was most highly expressed in Cluster 4 (75%), showing significant differences between the four subtypes with a P-value of 0.035. The expression of programmed death-1 (PD-1) was highest in Cluster 1 (51%), with a P-value of 0.022. Vascular invasion occurred most frequently in Cluster 2 (28.9%), with a P-value of 0.022. The majority of patients with stage T3-4 were in Cluster 2 (67%), with a P-value of 0.003. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed significant differences in PFS between the four groups (P = 0.013). Among them, patients in Cluster 1 had the best prognosis, while those in Cluster 2 had the worst. CONCLUSION: This study highlights the effectiveness of consensus clustering analysis based on enhanced CT radiomics features in identifying associations between radiomics features, histopathological characteristics, and prognosis in different clusters. These findings provide valuable insights for clinicians in accurately and effectively evaluating the prognosis of esophageal cancer.
abstract_zh: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: 评估基于CT影像组学的共识聚类分析在食管鳞状细胞癌（ESC）患者风险分层及预测术后无进展生存期（PFS）中的效能。MATERIALS AND METHODS: 我们进行了一项回顾性研究，纳入2016年1月至2021年3月间诊断的546例ESC患者。所有患者均接受了术前增强CT检查。从增强CT图像中提取影像组学特征，并应用共识聚类算法基于这些特征对患者进行分组。采用统计学分析检验聚类结果与基因蛋白表达、组织病理学特征及患者3年PFS之间的关系。连续数据采用Kruskal-Wallis检验，分类数据采用卡方检验或Fisher精确检验，PFS采用log-rank检验。RESULTS: 本研究识别出四组：聚类1（n = 100，18.3%）、聚类2（n = 197，36.1%）、聚类3（n = 205，37.5%）和聚类4（n = 44，8.1%）。癌症基因乳腺癌易感基因1（BRCA1）在聚类4中表达最高（75%），四种亚型间差异显著，P值为0.035。程序性死亡受体-1（PD-1）在聚类1中表达最高（51%），P值为0.022。血管侵犯在聚类2中发生频率最高（28.9%），P值为0.022。T3-4期患者多数位于聚类2（67%），P值为0.003。Kaplan-Meier生存分析显示四组间PFS存在显著差异（P = 0.013）。其中，聚类1患者预后最佳，而聚类2患者预后最差。CONCLUSION: 本研究强调了基于增强CT影像组学特征的共识聚类分析在识别不同聚类中影像组学特征、组织病理学特征与预后之间关联的有效性。这些发现为临床医生准确、有效评估食管癌预后提供了宝贵见解。
